title: A reduced feeding circuit cut from FlyWire v783: every neuron sugar makes spike, checked spike for spike against the whole brain
preregistration: The regimes, seeds and criteria were written before any held-out run. The circuit is cut on the dev regime only (cut_trials per condition). A dev check with 5 trials found closure violations at 150-300 Hz and an engine-bound speedup of 10x; the cut trials were raised to 20 and the criteria rewritten, and a dev check of that cut passed all three (106 of 110 trials exact; 9 closure violations, none changing MN9 by more than the tolerance), before the held-out regime (rates, ramps and steps the dev regime lacks, and new seeds) ran. It runs once, from a clean commit, and is reported whatever it shows.
purpose: R.A.I.N. Genesis Stage C: a connectome module cheap enough to sit in a research fly's loop for a whole life in the ecology (docs/RAIN_GENESIS.md).

criteria.R1: primary: on every held-out condition, the reduced circuit's mean MN9 rate is within the readout tolerance of the whole brain's (2% of the whole brain's rate or 1 Hz, whichever is larger), under the same random draws
criteria.R2: at least min_exact_share of held-out trials equal the whole brain's spike counts on every kept neuron
criteria.R3: every held-out trial in which no neuron outside the cut spikes is exact (the cut's exactness argument holds)

limits_note: One process, on the machine the record names. Nothing here starts cloud compute.
cost_note: Wall time of both is recorded, in this engine. The cost that matters to a fly is the TypeScript engine's, judged by the ecology protocol that uses the circuit.
